image_description: A grey whale is captured in the ocean, with its tail flukes raised high out of the water, creating a splash. The visible portion shows the dark, mottled skin characteristic of the species, with white barnacle patches. The background consists of calm blue sea and a clear sky horizon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely submerged and not visible in the frame; only the tail and posterior body are shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the tail and back exhibits the correct mottled grey/black coloration with distinct white irregular patches consistent with barnacle colonies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the back leading to the tail shows a series of small humps (knuckles) rather than a single prominent dorsal fin, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the posterior third of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified due to occlusion by water and framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; the texture and pattern on the visible body parts are accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Baleen plates are located inside the mouth/head area, which is submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the anterior/mid-body and are submerged/not visible in this tail-fluke shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are clearly visible, showing a broad structure with a distinct central notch and smooth edges, consistent with cetacean anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface of the tail and back appears textured and uneven, consistent with the rough skin and callosities/barnacles described.
